Top candidates:
- **Charcoal_Rot**: "numerous tiny, black microsclerotia scattered throughout the pith"
- **Diaporthe**: "linear rows of black specks (pycnidia) on mature soybean stems"

The specks appear scattered rather than in linear rows — favoring Charcoal_Rot. Let me confirm with the reference.

The reference confirms: Charcoal Rot shows a gray/charcoal stem surface with scattered microsclerotia throughout the pith when viewed up close. The test image is a microscope view showing exactly this — numerous tiny black microsclerotia randomly scattered across light-colored stem/pith tissue, not in linear rows (which would indicate Diaporthe).
